correctness.rationale: For q≥2, any r lines cover at most rq+1 points, and equality at r=q+1 forces a pencil. Duality gives the same bound for line vertices. Since each openly dominated color class lies on one bipartition side, at least q+1 classes are necessary on each side. At equality, the q offcenter points of each pencil line are forced into its class; they determine that line uniquely. Only the common pencil center may move among point classes, and only the dual pencil line among line classes. This gives exact labels, counts and v² copies of K_{q+1} □ K_{q+1}. Independent exhaustive class-partition search and a separate constructive exchange checker agree for q=2,3; finite cases do not replace the quantified proof.

value.rationale: Projective-plane incidence graphs form a canonical infinite family of sparse regular girth-six graphs, including non-Desarguesian cases. Characterizing all equality configurations and their single-vertex reconfiguration graph answers the natural question of whether optimal class partitions can be reconfigured without relaxing the optimum. The two frozen pencil centers and disconnected K_m Cartesian K_m components are structurally meaningful, independent of the already-known scalar chromatic number.
